So snow is in the forecast for this weekend. Where I live, anything close to an inch of accumulation shuts everything down. Any more than that and we can expect to lose power for a couple days. The snow isn't the probelm, the ice is. Our snow always starts with rain which ends up being a nice layer of ice under the snow. Of course, the ice also sticks to the trees which is bad news for power lines. With that in mind, I need to do some bulk cooking so we can more easily have something to eat in the event we do lose power. I also have to go get groceries today before everyone starts to panic and cleans out the shelves.

We have peas and cornbread left over from last night's meal. I am going to make another batch of corn bread so that I can use that and last night's to make a nice batch of cornbread stuffing

I am also going to do a pork roast today. Just before christmas I picked up a couple whole boneless pork loins for cheap. I cut those whole loins into 3 seperate parts, two roasts, and usually take the center third and cut it into chops. We had some of the chops last night, so today I am going to cook one of the roasts. That will provide meat for tonight's meal and we can have sandwiches over the weekend.

Also doing a big pot of green beans seasoned with country ham.

If the forcast stays on track for snow, I will do another big batch of cooking tomorrow. More than likely it will be some kind of soup or beans. I will need to figure it out before I go get groceries.
Assuming you have some way to heat food (fireplace, bbq etc) I'd suggest beef stew and chilli. Makes you want to look forward to power outages.
